text:
samira.khan: Auditor sent a follow-up: we need step-by-step reproducible evidence exports for three cases: RBAC change, KMS key rotation, and vuln->incident. They want exact commands, storage paths, checksum+signature process, and which SOC2/ISO control IDs each artifact maps to.

audit-bot: I can auto-generate a list of candidate artifacts if owners confirm locations. @daniel.perez @olivia_w can you confirm?

daniel.perez: I'll take RBAC and the packaging of artifacts. Quick notes: we keep a canonical manifest, uploader identity, and object-lock when bundle is finalized. For RBAC changes the workflow is PR -> infra apply -> runtime audit log slice -> k8s subject snapshot.

olivia_w: I'll take KMS and vuln/incident. For KMS, we export key metadata, key policy, CloudTrail events, and the service-level encryption-context traces. For incidents, we include ticket export, CI artifact hash, deploy trace, and monitoring alert snapshots.

samira.khan: Please include the exact commands you run and the S3 paths we should expect. Also note retention windows and who signs the manifest.

daniel.perez: RBAC export (example AWS + k8s):

```bash
# export terraform plan JSON
terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > /tmp/tfplan.json

# slice CloudTrail for IAM events for timeframe
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/aws/cloudtrail/Redwood" \
  --filter-pattern "CreateUser|DeleteUser|AttachRolePolicy|PutRolePolicy|UpdateAssumeRolePolicy" \
  --start-time 1700000000000 --end-time 1700000360000 > /tmp/iam_events.json

# export k8s rolebindings and serviceaccounts
kubectl get rolebinding,clusterrolebinding -o yaml --all-namespaces > /tmp/rolebindings.yaml
kubectl get sa --all-namespaces -o yaml > /tmp/serviceaccounts.yaml
```

 daniel.perez: Upload layout: s3://audit-exports/rbac/{ticket}/{ts}/tfplan.json, iam_events.json, rolebindings.yaml, serviceaccounts.yaml, approvals.pdf, manifest.txt.asc. We compute SHA256 for each file and create manifest.txt with lines "SHA256  filename" then sign with GPG: 

```bash
sha256sum /tmp/* > /tmp/manifest.txt
gpg --local-user daniel@redwood --armor --detach-sign /tmp/manifest.txt
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.txt s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/$TS/manifest.txt
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.txt.asc s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/$TS/manifest.txt.asc
```

olivia_w: KMS rotation export (example AWS):

```bash
# describe key metadata
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/prod-data > /tmp/key_meta.json

# export key policy
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/prod-data --policy-name default > /tmp/key_policy.json

# CloudTrail events for key management
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/aws/cloudtrail/Redwood" \
  --filter-pattern "CreateKey|EnableKey|DisableKey|RevokeGrant|ScheduleKeyDeletion|RotateKey" \
  --start-time 1700000000000 --end-time 1700000360000 > /tmp/kms_events.json

# service envelope evidence (example S3 encryption-context listing)
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-encrypted-backups --query 'Contents[?contains(Key, `enc-`)]' > /tmp/encrypted_backups.json
```

olivia_w: KMS upload path: s3://audit-exports/kms/{key_alias}/{ts}/key_meta.json, key_policy.json, kms_events.json, encrypted_backups.json, manifest.txt, manifest.txt.asc. Note: we also add key-id and key-arn into manifest and store a copy of the KMS policy as of export for reviewer validation.

olivia_w: Incident evidence export (vuln->incident):

```bash
# ticket export (example Jira)
curl -u $JIRA_API_TOKEN "https://redwood.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/$TICKET" > /tmp/ticket.json

# CI artifact SHA
sha256sum build/output/artifact.tar.gz > /tmp/artifact.sha256

# deployment trace
curl -s "https://deploy.internal/api/v1/deploys/$DEPLOY_ID/trace" > /tmp/deploy_trace.json

# monitoring alerts snapshot (Prometheus)
curl -g "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=ALERTS&start=1700000000&end=1700000360" > /tmp/alerts.json

# slack transcript (redacted)
/compliance/export_slack --channel incident-bridge --start 1700000000 --end 1700000360 > /tmp/slack_raw.txt
python3 /tools/redact_slack.py /tmp/slack_raw.txt /tmp/slack_redacted.txt
```

olivia_w: Incident upload path: s3://audit-exports/incidents/{ticket}/{ts}/ticket.json, artifact.sha256, deploy_trace.json, alerts.json, slack_redacted.txt, manifest.txt, manifest.txt.asc. We tag the S3 objects with uploader, job-id, and note whether raw transcript was redacted and where raw is locked.

samira.khan: How long are these artifacts kept and where do they live for long-term retrieval? Also how do you demonstrate immutability?

daniel.perez: Hot retention: 365 days. Cold: archived to Glacier Deep for 7 years with S3 Object Lock GOVERNANCE applied on finalized bundles. We keep an audit index that records object key, SHA256, signer, upload time, and object-lock ID.

olivia_w: Chain-of-custody: uploader runs sha256sum, signs manifest (GPG), CI job that uploaded also records the job run id into object metadata. SecOps approvals are recorded as part of the ticket and we include screen grabs or ticket change history in the bundle. For KMS bundles we include the KMS key used to encrypt the bundle object and the key policy snapshot.

samira.khan: Final ask from auditor: map each artifact to the control IDs (SOC2 CC6.1, CC6.2, ISO 27001 A.9.2.3, etc.) and provide one sample RBAC bundle and one sample KMS bundle for reproduction. Can you prepare and attach to AUD-2026-450?

daniel.perez: I'll prepare a sample RBAC bundle and a template manifest and push to compliance repo under examples/audit-bundles/ by EOD.

olivia_w: I'll prepare KMS and incident templates and attach them to the same ticket.

audit-bot: Created audit task AUD-2026-450. Verification window scheduled 2026-04-07 15:00 UTC.

samira.khan: Thanks team. Ping me once the PRs and sample bundles are available.
